messages:
jess: heads-up — hitting a weird HF->Redwood tokenizer mismatch during new model bring-up. conversion succeeded but runtime errors on start. anyone seen missing tokenizer.json vs tokenizer_config.json issues?

omar: can you paste the exact runtime error? my gut says fast vs slow tokenizer mismatch. Redwood conversion expects a fast tokenizer (tokenizer.json) for caching and token-id stability.

srinivas: +1, fast vs slow is usually the culprit. also check special tokens (bos/eos/pad) — chat templates rely on them.

jess: error log: 
```
RuntimeError: Tokenizer missing: expected tokenizer.json but only found tokenizer_config.json and vocab files.
Failed to initialize PreTrainedTokenizerFast: no "tokenizer.json" present.
During request: invalid token ids for chat template, missing <|system|> mapping.
```
Steps I took: clone HF repo, AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(local_dir) -> redwood-convert --model local_dir --out redwood_pkg -> upload to staging -> start model -> crash on init.

omear: (typo -> omar) meant: if the HF model originally ships only a python "slow" tokenizer (e.g., GPT2Tokenizer) you won't get tokenizer.json on save unless you export a fast tokenizer. Transformers usually create a PreTrainedTokenizerFast only if the original tokenizer has a tokenizers-backed implementation.

eva: do you know which HF repo this is? some community models have tokenizer_config.json that lists special tokens but no fast tokenizer. chat templates then look for tokens named in tokenizer_config.json but the runtime code glues them to ids using tokenizer.json. mismatch = bad.

jess: model is community/gpt-chat-mini (private fork). tokenizer_config.json contains: 
```json
{
  "bos_token": "<|bos|>",
  "eos_token": "<|eos|>",
  "unk_token": "<|unk|>"
}
```
but there is no tokenizer.json, only merges/vocab.json and added_tokens.json.

srinivas: quick workaround: load with the fast tokenizer and re-save. e.g. 
```bash
python - <<'PY'
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
t = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('path/to/local', use_fast=True)
# if use_fast fails because mapping not available, try tokenizers library to build one
t.save_pretrained('path/to/out')
print('saved', 'path/to/out')
PY
```
That will write tokenizer.json if a fast tokenizer backend is available.

omar: if AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(..., use_fast=True) throws because no fast impl exists, another pattern is to build a tokenizers.Tokenizer wrapper from vocab/merges and then export to tokenizer.json. e.g.: 
```python
from tokenizers import Tokenizer, models, trainers, pre_tokenizers
# reconstruct from vocab/merges (example for BPE)
# serialize to tokenizer.json then t = PreTrainedTokenizerFast(tokenizer_file='tokenizer.json')
```
But that's a bit manual.

jess: tried use_fast=True — it falls back to slow and save_pretrained writes tokenizer_config + vocab only. so convert tool ends up packaging only tokenizer_config.json and runtime fails.

eva: two short-term fixes: (1) teach redwood-convert to detect absence of tokenizer.json and attempt to synthesize one (best-effort) from vocab/merges/merges.txt + tokenizer_config.json; (2) update onboarding docs to require models to include a tokenizer.json for Redwood ingestion.

srinivas: agree. also note chat templates expect named special tokens. Even if we synth a tokenizer.json, we must ensure token ids of special tokens are stable. So the conversion should: parse added_tokens.json and tokenizer_config.json, ensure pad/bos/eos/sep/cls map exist in added_tokens and create them deterministically if missing (append to vocab). Document that this will change ids from HF default if HF later adds a fast tokenizer — potential risk.

omar: I'll open a tiny PR for redwood-convert that: 
- checks for tokenizer.json;
- if missing, tries AutoTokenizer(..., use_fast=True) -> save_pretrained(temp) -> include tokenizer.json;
- if use_fast not available, emit a clear validation error telling user how to create tokenizer.json with the tokenizers lib.
PR will include code snippets and tests for a toy BPE repo.

jess: that sounds perfect — thanks. for immediate unblock I regenerated a tokenizer.json locally with tokenizers and uploaded a patched package to staging. model boots now but I'll run evals to confirm no chat template regressions.

eva: nice. can you add the failing repo link and conversion logs to the onboarding ticket? ticket #ML-482.

jess: added logs + staging package link. marking as follow-up for the PR. :thumbsup:

tokenizer-bot: automated note: reproduced conversion failure on model community/gpt-chat-mini at 1782468125. Created temporary artifact s3://redwood-staging/tokenizer-fix-1782468125.zip.

srinivas: small follow-up: we should also surface a warning in Console when a model package lacks tokenizer.json and chat templates are enabled. Prevents silent runtime failures.

omar: agreed — Console warning and convert-time validation. I'll add both to the PR checklist.

jess: thanks team — will run quantization/ops suite after evals pass.
